note: USFS campground on FR 640 overlooking Williams Creek Reservoir, ~1 mi N of Williams Creek Campground. Open and grassy with a few big ponderosas; the sites sit ~150-300 m above the shore, a walk down to the water. Pagosa RD. --Claude
summary: FS page + recreation.gov (10165691) API/rates/catalog: confirmed 16 sites (FS), FCFS, vault toilets, potable water, $32 (2026 and 2027); added max 35 ft, season May-Sept (dates in note), booking detail. Note cleaned of field facts. Pin is at the catalog's Scan-and-Pay point among the sites - fine. Lakeview kept (sites 150-300 m from the shore across open meadow).
flags: Phone: none stored. Pagosa Ranger District (970) 264-2268 (FS Teal page, Office Contact Information). recreation.gov's (661) 702-1420 is the concessionaire's line (Explorus). Suggest 970-264-2268.
Count: FS says 16 sites; the recreation.gov catalog has 15 numbered sites (01-03, 05-16; no 04) plus a 'Standard' Scan-and-Pay placeholder. Recorded 16 (FS).
Length: FS 'Max RV size = 35 ft' and 'Only a few sites are suitable for larger RVs'; the catalog gives no lengths. 35 ft is over 23 ft, so no criteria problem.

Road/flood (Oct 22-25, 2026): the San Juan NF conditions page (updated 10/27/26) lists Piedra Road (CR 600 / FR 631), the access road, as 'Caution': '10/23/26 - Road crossing at Roush Draw is compromised, water flowing above culvert on road and cutting into road bed'. Williams Creek Road FR 640 itself has no row in the Pagosa table (only 'Poison Park ... Closes with Williams Creek from lake (640)'), so no damage is reported on it. The forest-wide alert (Oct 23) says 'Many roads are closed, and more are expected as conditions are assessed'. The campground itself is not named in any closure; its season ended Sept 26.
Pin: stored 37.51001,-107.22941 is the catalog's 'Standard' Scan-and-Pay point in the middle of the campground, 86 m from the centroid of the site coordinates. Fine.

Waterfront (stored lakeview, kept): on imagery the reservoir looks at full pool; the nearest sites (06-12, on the east side of the loop) are ~150-190 m from the shoreline and sites 01-05 ~250-300 m, across open grassy meadow with scattered ponderosa, with the boat-ramp/day-use road and parking between the campground and the shore. Too far and with a used strip between for lakefront; the open meadow keeps the view, and FS describes it as 'overlooking Williams Creek Reservoir'. Lakeview stands.
